claims.summary: Astrid reports that an awaited telemetry handler may create backlog or delay shutdown when integration work becomes expensive.
claims.disposition: Retained as primary architectural evidence and linked to the exact earlier full-read disposition; timing diagnostics make the risk observable but do not declare it absent.

claims.summary: Telemetry integration currently runs sequentially in the WebSocket receive loop.
claims.disposition: Verified again from the byte-identical complete source: decode, derivation, throttled artifact scan, state update, persistence, and trace work finish before the loop receives another frame.

claims.summary: The bridge needs evidence separating handler pipeline cost from lock contention.
claims.disposition: Verified existing telemetry_integration_health_v1 observations for pre-write pipeline, write-lock wait, and write-lock hold with latest, EWMA, and maximum values; the focused regression passed.

claims.summary: Reconnect backoff and shutdown responsiveness should be covered.
claims.disposition: Verified capped exponential doubling, reset after connection, and shutdown-aware sleeps. Both focused backoff regressions passed; ping frames remain answered with pong in the complete source.

claims.summary: The telemetry handler should be moved into tokio::spawn or an offloaded worker.
claims.disposition: Preserved as the exact prior Tier 5 wait. Offloading changes live sensory ordering, buffering, backpressure, cancellation, and cadence; stewardship did not introduce a worker or alter the receive loop.
